cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel, has the timber and the stone ready (1 Kings 5:18), and now he's about to build the house of the LORD. This is the BIG one, friend. The Bible dates this moment by counting all the way back to when Israel came out of Egypt.

Up goes the house: sixty cubits long, with a porch out front, narrow windows up high, and three floors of side rooms built all along its walls. But the quietest part of this job is how the stones get there.

cards.question: The stones for the temple are finished at the quarry before they ever reach the building site. What does that mean while the temple goes up?

answers.text: No iron tool is heard in the temple
The workers never have to leave Lebanon
The building is done in half the time

cards.text: A stairway climbs the side rooms, and the roof goes on with beams and planks of cedar. A whole temple built in near silence, and I've heard one man hang ONE shelf and it sounded like a drum solo.
Then the word of the LORD comes to Solomon about this temple he's building. Friend, when THAT happens, you stop what you're doing and you LISTEN.

cards.question: God says He'll fulfill through Solomon the promise He made to Solomon's father, David, but there's an 'if.' What does Solomon need to do?

answers.text: Keep all God's commandments and walk in them
Bring a thousand offerings to the new altar
Build the temple bigger than any palace

cards.question: Still speaking to Solomon about the temple, God says what He'll do for the Israelites. What does He promise?

answers.text: Dwell among them and not abandon them
Make them the greatest of all nations
Send them a new prophet every year

cards.text: So Solomon builds the temple and finishes it. Inside, cedar covers the walls, carved with gourds and open flowers, and not a stone can be seen. At the back, cedar boards wall off an inner room: the Most Holy Place.

cards.question: Solomon prepares the inner sanctuary as the place to set the ___ of the covenant of the LORD.

cards.text: Then come the finishing touches, all the way out to the inner courtyard. Two olive wood cherubim stand in the Most Holy Place with their wingtips touching in the middle, carved doors open into it, and GOLD covers the whole interior. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer under a takeout menu, and this man's got GOLD on the inside.
The foundation went down in the fourth year of Solomon's reign, in the month of Ziv. Then in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, the eighth month, the work wraps up.

cards.question: In the end, the temple is finished according to every specification.

cards.text: Keep that apron on, friend. This story's still in the oven.
